## Force the appliance on by hand

Every appliance gets a **Force on** switch, `switch.<name>_force_on`. Turn it on and the appliance runs right away, on top of everything: the plan, the prices, an unreachable API. Turn it off and the plan takes over again at once, so the appliance stops if it is outside a planned slot. It replaces the `input_boolean` and the automation of a hand-made "force" setup.

- It works without an entity to control: `binary_sensor.<name>` turns `on` and carries `boost_active: true`.
- The *Automatic control* switch still wins: while it is off, the appliance is left alone.
- It survives a Home Assistant restart, and never arms the consumption hold.

## Not on days with a negative price

*Always run below this price* can now be left out on the days that hold a negative price. Tick **Not on days with a negative price** on an appliance: any day (midnight to midnight) with at least one negative price runs the slots the plan selected and nothing more. A price of exactly `0` is not negative. `sobry.get_cheapest_slots` takes the same `force_skip_negative`.

## Changed

- **The consumption hold only applies after the last window of the day.** *Keep running while this entity draws power* used to extend every planned window. An earlier window now ends as planned, whatever the appliance still draws; the hold applies at the end of the last one, after any *extra runtime*. For an overnight window, the day is that window. A fallback schedule is a single run, so it is still held.

Existing appliances need no other change: the new option is off by default, and the force switch appears on its own, switched off.
